**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Termination for convenience (T4C)**

**What the document says.** Section 11 binds Corio to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals (¶p0096). The only exit rights are material breach after a 30-day cure and immediate insolvency termination (¶p0097), supplemented by narrow remedies elsewhere (acceptance-test failure in §3, uncorrectable warranty breach in §7, IP-infringement fallback in §8).

**Why it fails.** There is no Corio right to terminate for convenience anywhere in a multi-year term — the playbook's walk-away scenario. The 30-day notice in 11.1 is only a non-renewal notice at the end of a term, not a mid-term exit. This is the "missing behaviour" case in the detection guidance.

**Direction check.** Commerce One has no convenience right either, so the counterparty side of the rule is already satisfied; the redline is purely additive in our favour and does not reopen the term commitment or pricing.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** New §11.1A inserted after ¶p0096: Corio may terminate in whole or in part on 30 days' prior written notice, without penalty or early-termination charge, with refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period, and confirming Commerce One has no convenience right — the preferred position, with 60 days offered as a fallback in the comment.
